title: Meeting Charlie Johnson in Atlantic City
summary: Wooding calls Charlie Johnson of Boston a great early help, and says Johnson later partnered with Weloff to open the Paradise.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Anyhow, so I stayed with this girl, but I had a chance now of meeting one of the greatest men that helped me in my life. That was a fellow called Charlie Johnson. Charlie Johnson was about three or four years older than I was, but he come from Boston. He taught me a lot of things. The fact that I hadn't had before, in the early years, before, you know.
Did he have a band at that time?
Oh, at that time didn't nobody have a band in Atlantic City. They had some combinations. I think he was working with a tenor banjo player and a drummer, you see.
Was the Paradise open at that point?
No, no, this was way before that.
It was before the Paradise, huh?
Just played around any way he could, you know? And, afterwards, he got with Ray Weloff, and they opened the Paradise. But, at that time, there wasn't any Paradise, see?
What year are we talking about, now?
This was just before the war, '15 or '16, now.
